test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Three persons P, Q, and R started a business with their shares in the ratio 11 : 8 : 20. After 9 months, Q withdrew his 35% share, while R withdrew his 14% share 7 months prior to completion of the year. If the total profit at the end of the year is ₹40,700, find the share of R (in ₹) in the profit.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Profit = Σ(Investment × Time).

P share = 11 × 12 = 132 units.

Q share = (8 × 9) + (8 × 0.65 × 3) = 72 + 15.6 = 87.6 units.

R share = (20 × 5) + (20 × 0.86 × 7) = 100 + 120.4 = 220.4 units.

Total units = 132 + 87.6 + 220.4 = 440 units.

R share = (220.4 ÷ 440) × 40,700 = 20,387.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹20,387.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Investment Ratio **P : Q : R = 11 : 8 : 20**. Total time = **12 months**.
Formulas: Profit Ratio = (I₁ × T₁) : (I₂ × T₂) : (I₃ × T₃)
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e2dc24202d73447ebcd21f3672a791ea5cc6a1fd7f45c1eaeebefce6456f2a1a.png] 
⇒ **P's Profit** = 11 × 12 = 132.
⇒ **Q's Profit**: Q withdraws 35% after 9 months. Remaining = 65% of 8 = 5.2.
⇒ Q Total = (8 × 9) + (5.2 × 3) = 72 + 15.6 = 87.6.
⇒ **R's Profit**: R withdraws 14% 7 months prior to completion (at 5 months). Remaining = 86% of 20 = 17.2.
⇒ R Total = (20 × 5) + (17.2 × 7) = 100 + 120.4 = 220.4.
⇒ Total Ratio Sum = 132 + 87.6 + 220.4 = 440.
⇒ **Share of R** = (220.4 ÷ 440) × 40,700 = 0.500909... × 40,700 = 20,387.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹20,387.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Basics

In a partnership, the profit is distributed in the ratio of the product of **investment** and **time period**.

Variable Investment

If an investor changes the capital during the period, calculate **Equivalent Capital** for 1 month by summing (Capital × Duration) for each segment.
